title: Acute leg weakness
stem: Cubicle 6. Mr Ng, 28, woke this morning unable to stand; both legs are weak. He was well last night after a big dinner and drinks with friends. Take a focused history and discuss your differential and management.

review.text: Age. Your notes present a 70-year-old with hypokalaemic periodic paralysis. Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis is typically a young East Asian man; in an older patient, look first for diuretics, GI losses or other causes of low potassium.

Treatment detail for thyrotoxic periodic paralysis: small doses of potassium only (for example 10 mmol/h), because it shifts back out of cells and can cause rebound hyperkalaemia; propranolol treats the cause and the paralysis.

notes:
Checked against endocrine and neurology references on thyrotoxic periodic paralysis (TPP; common in young East Asian men) and the ED approach to acute flaccid weakness (cord compression, Guillain–Barré, myasthenia, stroke, electrolyte disorders).

TPP: sudden proximal weakness, often after carbohydrate-rich meals, alcohol or rest after exercise, with hypokalaemia from intracellular shift (not total-body deficit) caused by thyrotoxicosis. Treat carefully: small doses of potassium (e.g. 10 mmol/h IV or oral) because of rebound hyperkalaemia when the shift reverses; non-selective beta-blocker (propranolol) treats the cause and the paralysis; then treat the thyrotoxicosis. Monitor ECG and potassium.

Your notes present a 70-year-old with 'hypokalaemic periodic paralysis (age-related or thyrotoxic triggers)'. Primary periodic paralysis usually starts in youth; in an older patient think more of diuretics, GI losses, or other causes. The rest matches. Red flags for cord compression (back pain, sensory level, sphincter disturbance) must be screened in every case.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Onset, distribution, triggers, red flags, thyroid symptoms, family and drug history.

Weakness.t: When did it start and how has it changed?
Weakness.tz: 幾時開始？之後有咩變化？
Weakness.rz: 朝早六點醒嗰陣已經係咁。而家好返少少。
Weakness.r: Woke up at 6 like this. Getting a little better now.

Weakness.t: Which parts are weak — legs, arms, face, breathing, swallowing?
Weakness.tz: 邊度冇力——對腳、對手、塊面？呼吸同吞嘢有冇問題？
Weakness.rz: 兩隻腳，主要係大髀。手都有少少。呼吸同吞嘢冇問題。
Weakness.r: Both legs, mostly thighs. Arms a bit. Breathing and swallowing fine.
Weakness.mark: Asks distribution including bulbar and respiratory

Red flags.t: Back pain, injury, problems passing urine or opening bowels?
Red flags.tz: 有冇背痛、受傷？小便大便有冇問題？
Red flags.rz: 冇背痛，冇受傷，大小便正常。
Red flags.r: No back pain, no injury, bladder and bowel normal.

Red flags.tz: 最近有冇肚屙或者感染？

Triggers.t: What did you do last night?
Triggers.rz: 食咗餐豐富晚飯——飯、麵、甜品——仲飲咗幾罐啤酒。
Triggers.r: Big dinner — rice, noodles, dessert — and several beers.
Triggers.mark: Asks about carbohydrate meal and alcohol triggers

Triggers.rz: 舊年試過一次，輕啲，自己好返。
Triggers.r: Once last year, milder, went away by itself.

Thyroid.t: Weight loss, palpitations, sweating, heat intolerance, tremor?
Thyroid.tz: 有冇瘦咗、心跳、出汗多、怕熱、手震？
Thyroid.rz: 三個月瘦咗五公斤，成日覺得熱，有時心跳好快。
Thyroid.r: Lost 5 kg in 3 months, feel hot, heart races sometimes.

Background.tz: 有冇食藥？屋企人有咩病？有冇飲酒、用藥物？
Background.rz: 冇食藥。舅父有甲狀腺問題。冇用藥物。
Background.r: No medicines. Uncle had thyroid problems. No drugs.

Now.r: Sinus tachycardia 108, flattened T waves, prominent U waves.

Now.t: TSH and free T4, CK, magnesium, phosphate

steps.ask: Thank you. What do you think is going on, and what is your plan?
steps.label: Discuss
steps.hint: Diagnosis, careful potassium, propranolol, monitoring, endocrinology.

opts.t: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis; differentials: GBS, cord compression, myasthenia, other hypokalaemia
Cautious potassium replacement (small doses) with cardiac monitoring and repeat K every 1–2 h
Propranolol to reverse the shift; endocrinology referral for Graves' treatment

opts.r: The potassium shifts back out as the attack ends: aggressive replacement causes rebound hyperkalaemia.

qs.q: Risk of treating TPP with large potassium doses?

wrong: No beta-blocker; calcium channel blocker instead
Proximal weakness only, with normal reflexes

badge.name: Shifty K
badge.flavor: Young man, big meal, weak legs, low K: check the thyroid, go gently.

cards.q: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis is most common in…
cards.why: Often the first sign of Graves' disease.

options: Carbohydrate-rich meals, alcohol, rest after exercise
Flat T waves, U waves, ST depression
Tall peaked T waves with a widened QRS complex
A short QT interval with tall P waves
Rapid high-dose IV replacement to 5.0 mmol/L
Oral only, starting after 24 hours of rest
